To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ACK-based protocols are more efficient than the NAK-based and the tree-based ones for the Ethernet environment, and that the ring-based protocols are more suitable than the ACK-based ones to support reliable multicast over a single Ethernet.
reliable multicast protocols over LANs can provide higher communication performance than the standard reliable unicast protocols, and that the ACK-based protocol is the best choice for LANs.

the performance of the ACK-based protocols can be improved by exploiting the broadcast feature of Ethernet and the performance of the NAK-based, ring-based and tree-based protocols can be greatly improved by exploiting the multicast feature of Ethernet.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) the impact of the special features of the LANs on the performance of reliable multicast protocols; (2) how to design efficient reliable multicast protocols that exploit these features to maximize performance; and (3) how to evaluate the performance of reliable multicasting protocols.

the following issues: (1) the impact of the Ethernet on multicast performance, (2) the design of reliable multicast protocols for the Ethernet, and (3) the evaluation of the performance of the proposed protocols.
the following issues: - How to implement reliable multicast protocols over the standard IP multicasting mechanism using the standard UDP socket interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ACK-based protocol performs the best in terms of throughput, while the tree-based protocol is best in terms of message delivery ratio.
reliable multicast protocols are very effective for high-performance message passing over LANs, especially over Ethernet-connected LANs.
the ring-based protocol, the tree-based protocol and the ACK-based protocol with the selective ACK mechanism are the most efficient protocols for Ethernet-connected networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reliable multicast protocols over LANs can achieve high performance, and the performance is significantly improved if the protocol can be tuned to exploit the special features of the LANs.
the ring-based protocols can provide reliable communication with low latency, while the tree-based protocols can provide high throughput.
the tree-based protocols are the most efficient ones, the ring-based and the NAK-based ones are the least efficient ones, and the ACK-based protocols have a medium level performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for reliable multicast protocols over LANs, the use of the Ethernet multicast addresses can achieve higher performance and lower overhead than the use of the IP multicast addresses.
the performance of reliable multicast protocols is highly dependent on the network environment.
, for the reliable multicast protocols, the performance of the ring-based protocols is the best, followed by the NAK-based protocol with polling and then by the ACK-based protocols.
